blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Brain tumor segmentation uses complementary magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) sequences, but some sequences may be unavailable in practice. Their absence changes the information available for segmenting different tumor regions. Fusion methods can support different input subsets. However, fusion at several scales does not by itself specify how tumor evidence is retained and updated to guide fusion at later stages. We propose a progressive multi-scale tumor-state memory network (PMTM) for segmentation from any non-empty subset of T1ce, T1, FLAIR, and T2. PMTM maintains a compact state for the current subject across the encoder stages. At each stage, we use assignment maps to pool spatial features into ordered evidence vectors for each available modality. We average these vectors across the available modalities, and a learned gate combines this evidence with the previous state. The up- dated state guides residual fusion at that stage and is used in the state update at the next stage. A modality-token mixer also models interactions among the available modalities at each stage. We apply semantic supervision to the assignment maps at all four stages. We evaluate PMTM on BraTS2018, BraTS2020, and BraTS2023 GLI across all 15 non-empty modality subsets. Averaged over the three tumor regions and the 15 subsets, PMTM achieves Dice scores of 75.31%, 77.54%, and 80.47% on BraTS2018, BraTS2020, and BraTS2023 GLI, respectively. These scores are higher than those of RobustSeg, RFNet, and mmFormer in our experiments on each dataset. Component ablations and internal state analysis are performed on BraTS2020.
blocks.zh: 脑瘤分化使用互补的磁共振成像(MRI)序列,但实际上有些序列可能无法使用. 它们的缺失改变了可用于分解不同肿瘤区域的信息。 融合法可以支持不同的输入子集. 然而,几个尺度的聚变本身并不说明肿瘤证据如何被保留和更新,以指导后期的聚变. 我们提议建立一个渐进式多尺度肿瘤状态记忆网络(PMTM),用于从T1ce,T1,FLAIR,和T2等非空子集分出. PMTM在整个编码器阶段为当前主体保持了紧凑状态. 在每一个阶段,我们使用任务地图,将空间特征汇集到每种可用方式的有序证据矢量中。 我们平均这些矢量跨越可用的模式,一个有学识的门将这个证据与以前的状态结合. 最新状态指导了该阶段的残留聚变,并在下一阶段的状态更新中使用. 一个模式键混合器还模拟每个阶段现有模式之间的相互作用。 我们对所有四个阶段的任务图实行语义学监督. BratS2018、BratS2020和BratS2023 GLI上所有15个非空模式子集的PMTM评价。 PMTM平均在3个肿瘤区域和15个子集中,在BratS2018,BratS2020和BratS2023GLI上分别取得了75.31%,77.54%和80.47%的Dice分数. 我们在每个数据集的实验中,这些分数都高于RobustSeg、RFNet和mmFormer。 BRATS2020进行了组件分解和内部状态分析。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Glioma segmentation on MRI supports diagnosis and treatment
planning [ Jyothi & Singh, 2023 ] .
The tumor regions considered here are the whole tumor (WT),
tumor core (TC), and enhancing tumor (ET) [ Menze et al., 2015 , Bakas et al., 2017 ] .
To identify these regions, multimodal brain MRI commonly combines
contrast-enhanced T1-weighted (T1ce), T1-weighted (T1),
fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR), and T2-weighted (T2)
images [ Menze et al., 2015 , Bakas et al., 2017 ] .
These sequences provide complementary information about the
tumor regions. T1ce is especially informative for TC and ET,
while FLAIR and T2 provide information about edema and WT [ Ding et al., 2021 , Xiao et al., 2025 ] .

blocks.en:
Many multimodal segmentation models are designed to receive a complete
set of MRI sequences [ Zhou et al., 2023 ] .
However, differences in acquisition protocols, image corruption,
resource constraints, and restrictions on contrast administration
can leave one or more sequences unavailable [ Zhou et al., 2023 ] .
The resulting loss of information affects tumor regions differently [ Ding et al., 2021 , Xiao et al., 2025 ] .
Segmentation from incomplete inputs therefore requires a fusion
mechanism that works with the available subset and accounts for
the information supplied by each remaining sequence.

Existing approaches address this problem in different ways.
Latent aggregation constructs a common representation from different
modality subsets [ Havaei et al., 2016 , Dorent et al., 2019 ] .
Region-aware fusion accounts for how each sequence contributes
to individual tumor regions [ Ding et al., 2021 ] .
Transformer modules learn interactions between modality
representations [ Y. Zhang et al., 2022 , Shi et al., 2024 ] .
Our earlier method, TG-BWSA, exchanges modality features between
encoder stages through a shared adapter [ Rostamian et al., 2026 ] .
These mechanisms determine how the available features are combined.
A related question is how evidence about tumor regions can be
accumulated across encoder stages and used to guide fusion
at later stages.

blocks.en:
We propose PMTM, a progressive multi-scale tumor-state memory network.
PMTM maintains a tumor state, an ordered set of feature vectors
called state slots.
At each encoder stage, assignment maps pool features from each
available modality into evidence vectors.
We average corresponding evidence vectors across the available
modalities and use them to update the state.
The updated state guides fusion at the current stage and is used
in the state update at the next stage.
Fusion uses the current modality features together
with the state accumulated from preceding stages.
At the beginning of each forward pass, the state is initialized
from a learned tensor. State updates use evidence from the
available sequences of the current subject.

blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: 2.1 Fusion in complete multimodal brain tumor segmentation
blocks.zh: 2.1 完全多模式脑瘤分裂中的融合

blocks.en:
Methods for complete inputs differ in when MRI sequences are combined. Pereira et al. [2016] processed the four sequences jointly with
a patch-based CNN.
Separate encoders allow fusion to adjust modality contributions
after feature extraction. Zhou et al. [2020] use attention and tumor-region context
constraints, while Tri-Attention [ Zhou et al., 2022 ] weights
modality and spatial features and models correlations between sequences.

限制,而Tri-Attenty [周等人,2022]重量

blocks.en:
Transformer fusion models dependencies between modality
representations through attention.
NestedFormer [ Xing et al., 2022 ] uses intra-modality and
cross-modality attention at higher levels and modality-sensitive
gating at lower scales. Zhou et al. [2025] combine modality-wise, spatial, and
channel-wise feature fusion.
These designs adjust how features are combined for complete inputs.
With missing sequences, fusion must also accept different input subsets.

blocks.en: 2.2 Incomplete multimodal brain tumor segmentation
blocks.zh: 2.2 不完整的多模式脑瘤分裂

blocks.en:
Supporting different subsets first requires a representation that
can be constructed from the available inputs.
HeMIS [ Havaei et al., 2016 ] aggregates modality-specific features
through their mean and variance.
U-HVED [ Dorent et al., 2019 ] instead combines distributions inferred
from the available modalities in a probabilistic latent space
for joint segmentation and modality completion.
Beyond accepting different subsets, fusion can also adjust the
contribution of the remaining modalities.
RobustSeg [ Chen et al., 2019 ] separates shared and
modality-specific representations and applies gated fusion.
RFNet [ Ding et al., 2021 ] makes fusion region-aware, accounting
for differences in the information each sequence provides about
each tumor region.
D 2 -Net [ Yang et al., 2022 ] models modality and region relationships
through dual disentanglement.

blocks.en: 2.3 Memory mechanisms in medical image segmentation

blocks.en:
Memory provides context whose role depends on what is stored
and where it is reused.

hierarchically stacked gated convolutional units and across PET/CT
encoder branches.
HMDM-Net [ Z. Zhang et al., 2026 ] retains deep semantic representations
across decoder resolutions.
Memory-Net reuses intermediate information during feature extraction,
while HMDM-Net combines deep and shallow features during decoding.

of the current input.

relationships.
Its memory attention models correlations between modalities
and dependencies across slices.

a modality-adaptive fusion decoder.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en:
In this work, we develop PMTM for brain tumor segmentation from
incomplete multimodal MRI. We first describe the overall network
architecture, followed by the progressive tumor-state memory and
state-guided fusion with modality-token interaction. We then present
the modality sampling procedure and training objectives.

结构,然后是渐进的肿瘤状态记忆和
以模式键交互方式进行状态引导核聚变。 然后我们介绍
模式取样程序和培训目标。

blocks.en: 3.1 Network overview

blocks.en:
Figure 1 shows the overall architecture.
PMTM has four modality-specific encoders and a shared segmentation
decoder. The encoders have the same architecture but independent
parameters. Each encoder has four stages that produce feature maps
at different spatial scales.

blocks.en:
For the current subject, PMTM maintains a tumor state that stores
evidence from the available MRI sequences. At each encoder stage,
the available modality features update this state.
Each stage has a fusion module with state-guided fusion and
a modality-token mixer. The updated state guides feature fusion,
and the mixer models interactions among the available modalities.
The shared decoder
combines the fused features from all four stages and predicts
four segmentation classes.

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en:
We evaluate PMTM on BraTS2018, BraTS2020, and BraTS2023 GLI
across all 15 non-empty modality subsets. We first describe
the datasets, evaluation protocol, and implementation details.
We then compare PMTM with RobustSeg, RFNet, and mmFormer
trained in this study and with published BraTS2020 and BraTS2023
results [ Zou et al., 2026 , Z. Zhang et al., 2025 ] .
We also report component ablations, analyses of assignment maps
and tumor states, and segmentation maps under complete and
incomplete inputs.

blocks.en:
We use BraTS2018 and BraTS2020 [ Menze et al., 2015 , Bakas et al., 2017 , Bakas et al., 2018 ] , and the adult glioma
task of the BraTS 2023 Challenge (BraTS2023 GLI) [ BraTS 2023 Challenge, 2023 , Baid et al., 2021 , Baid et al., 2023 ] .
The training/validation/test splits contain 205/23/57,
219/50/100, and 875/125/251 subjects, respectively.
For BraTS2020, we use the public subject lists from the official
M 2 FTrans repository [ Shi et al., 2024 ] ; for BraTS2023 GLI,

blocks.en:

These observations are consistent with the different

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We developed PMTM for brain tumor segmentation from
incomplete multimodal MRI.
The method accumulates tumor evidence across encoder stages
and uses the updated state to guide modality fusion.
We evaluated PMTM on BraTS2018, BraTS2020, and BraTS2023 GLI
across all 15 non-empty modality subsets.
Dice averaged over the three tumor regions and all 15 subsets
is 75.31% on BraTS2018, 77.54% on BraTS2020,
and 80.47% on BraTS2023 GLI.
These averages are higher than those of RobustSeg, RFNet,
and mmFormer in our experiments on each dataset.
